kalejunkie HIDDEN VEGGIE PASTINA aka italian penicillin, the soup that cures all—sickness, a broken heart, and pays your bills for you too 😏. The real question is what can’t it do? This version sneaks in veggies for more fiber and flavor and if you have picky kids like me, they’ll never know it’s in there 🤝. 

SAVE this post! SHARE it with friends! And hello, FOLLOW ME kalejunkie if you want to see more easy delicious recipes in your feed (who wouldn’t, duh! 🙆🏻‍♀️)

Makes 6-8 servings
8 cups chicken broth (I used bone broth for more protein and nutrients!)
3 large carrots, peeled and halved
4 stalks celery, halved
1 yellow onion, roughly chopped
3 cloves garlic
2 tb betterthanbouillon chicken bouillon paste (or similar)
1 parmesan rind
2 bay leaves 
1 1/2 cups uncooked pastina (any small pasta shape like stelline or acini di pepe)
1 tsp turmeric
1 tsp kosher salt
1/2 cup freshly grated parmigiano reggiano cheese
Pepper and lemon juice to taste

In a large pot, add the broth, carrots, celery, onion, garlic, bouillon, parmesan rind, and bay leaves. Turn heat to medium-high. Bring to a gentle boil, then cover and reduce heat to medium and cook for 25 minutes or until carrots have softened. While the broth is cooking, bring another pot of water to a boil and cook pasta until al dente. Drain and set aside. Next, remove all the veggies from the pot and transfer to a blender. Add 1-2 cups of the broth as well as the turmeric and salt. Blend until smooth and return the mixture to the pot and stir until incorporated. To serve, divide the cooked pasta to bowls. Pour broth on top. Add lots of parmigiano reggiano cheese on top, black pepper and lemon juice. Enjoy!

Note: I cook the pasta separately and add at the time of serving. This way the pasta doesn’t soak up all the broth. Ho

INGREDIENTS:
1 small head green cabbage, cored and thinly sliced into ribbons
1 tablespoon olive oil, plus more as needed
Kosher salt, to taste
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 large egg
1/3 cup liquid egg whites
1/4 cup plain Greek yogurt
Freshly shaved or grated Parmesan cheese, for serving

RECIPE:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Spread the sliced cabbage on the baking sheet. Drizzle with the olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and toss to coat. Use a second baking sheet if needed to avoid crowding.
3. Roast for 15–20 minutes, tossing halfway through, until tender with lightly browned edges.
4. Meanwhile, whisk together the egg and egg whites in a bowl. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
5. Transfer the roasted cabbage to a large nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add a small drizzle of olive oil if needed to prevent sticking.
6. Pour the egg mixture over the cabbage. Cook, stirring and folding gently, until the eggs are fully set, about 3–5 minutes.
7. Remove the skillet from the heat and let stand for about 1 minute. Fold in the Greek yogurt until evenly combined.
8. Transfer to a bowl and finish with Parmesan and additional black pepper. Taste and adjust the salt before serving.

💡 3 tips for the best kabocha stir-fry:

🥢 Keep the pork juicy: Marinate the ground pork with sake, soy sauce, and potato starch for 5–10 minutes before cooking.

🎃 Don’t skip the microwave: Pre-cook the kabocha until about 80% tender. This helps it cook quickly in the pan without falling apart.

🌶️ Make it your own: Swap gochujang for miso if you prefer a non-spicy version, or use minced mushrooms instead of pork for a vegetarian option.

I’ve been wanting to post this for ages.  I know fasting can be controversial and that eating the right food to keep your immune system working is incredibly important when you have any illness, least of all cancer treatment but I really think there is something to this fasting business.

A school friend - who also only lost a bit of hair - put me onto prof_valterlongo when I was first diagnosed.  People offer so many solutions and health hacks when you are ill and there seems to be a whole industry around taking your money when you are desperate to do anything to get better….BUT I do think this theory is fascinating.
-
What I like about the Valter Longo team is that they are not for profit - so everything goes back into the research.  The book is a fascinating read into this cutting edge, very new adjunct therapy that you can combine with chemo to 

1. Make the chemo more effective against the cancer
2. Mitigate and lessen some of the really awful@side effects to nuking your body with poison and 
3. Give yourself some feeling of agency in the whole process.
-
I only know my own experience but the trials that have been done around fast mimicking diets and chemotherapy treatment are compelling. 

I know that I never actually threw up even when I felt my most nauseous.

I know that I have so far (touch wood) still got hair and eyebrows and eyelashes.

I know that I was able to get out and walk almost everyday of my treatment no matter how bad I felt.

I am a firm believer in the ancient adage that ‘Food is medicine.’ It clearly is or poor diets wouldn’t be linked to so much disease.  And fasting is an ancient practise.  What if fast mimicking diets did really help in the battle against cancer.  Def worth looking into from my perspective…

In my opinion, it’s not Thanksgiving unless there’s stuffing on the table!

Ingredients:

24 ounces bread, cut into ½-inch cubes (about 12 cups), preferably crusty sourdough or country bread
½ cup unsalted butter, plus 3 tablespoons for topping and for the pan
3 medium leeks, cleaned and chopped
5 celery stalks, diced
3 garlic cloves, chopped
¾ teaspoon sea salt
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
¼ cup chopped fresh sage
Heaping ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley
1 teaspoon chopped fresh rosemary
1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
3 cups vegetable broth, plus more as needed
2 large eggs, beaten

Instructions:

- Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with 1½ tablespoons of butter.
- Spread the bread cubes in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Bake for 10 to 25 minutes, or until dry and crisp. Remove from the oven and transfer to a large bowl.
- Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, garlic, salt, and pepper and cook for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until softened.
- Pour the onion mixture over the bread and sprinkle with the sage, parsley, rosemary, and thyme. Toss to coat. Add the broth and eggs and toss again. The bread should feel pretty wet. If it’s still a bit dry, add more broth as needed to moisten it. I often add another ¼ to ½ cup at this point.
- Transfer the mixture to the baking dish. Melt the remaining 1½ tablespoons of butter and drizzle over the stuffing. Bake, covered, for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake for 5 to 10 more minutes to crisp the top.

I post this every autumn. It looks meaty – and tastes it too – but there’s no meat or even any mushrooms in it, just the humble little lentil. The pasta is cooked with the lentils and the starch produces a kind of stew. Lovely - inexpensive too.

AUTUMN PASTA WITH LENTILS
SERVES 4

2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus a little extra for drizzling
1 medium onion, finely chopped
2 clove garlic, grated to a purée
¼ tsp chilli flakes
1 carrot, finely chopped
1 stick celery, finely chopped
225g green lentils, washed well in a sieve
1 tbsp tomato purée
2 bay leaves
4 sprigs thyme
400g can chopped tomatoes (I use Mutti polpa)
8 cherry tomatoes
250g macaroni, or another pasta shape of similar size
15g Parmigiano Reggiano, grated, plus extra for serving

Heat the oil in a large saucepan and sauté the onion for 5-8 minutes over a medium heat, until quite soft. It shouldn’t get too much colour. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for a couple of minutes more, then add the carrot, celery, lentils, tomato purée, herbs, seasoning and 1.2L water. Simmer the lentils, with the lid half off, for about 30 minutes. The lentils should keep their shape. Tip the can of tomatoes and the cherry tomatoes into the pan (leave the tomatoes whole to give a bit of texture and structure). Add the pasta, season again and add more water if you think the dish needs it.

Simmer for 10-15 minutes, uncovered, until the pasta is tender, stirring often so that the pasta releases its starch – you want to end up with a dish that is quite thick, not a soup. Add a little more water if you think the dish needs it.

Add the cheese and check the seasoning once more. Stir in some more extra virgin olive oil or drizzle it over individual servings. This can be reheated the next day – it still tastes great.
